literal.prompt: Какая воображаемая линия проходит через Антарктиду примерно на 66,5° южной широты?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NOAA explicitly names the Arctic Circle at about 66°N, Antarctic Circle at about 66°S, Tropic of Cancer around 23°N and Tropic of Capricorn around 23°S. AAP specifies the Antarctic Circle as 66°34′S. Given Antarctica and about 66.5°S, only the South Polar Circle matches.
literalGroups.locator: NOAA capture L12; AAP capture L315

literalGroups.literal: Это Южный полярный круг, проходящий примерно по 66,5° ю. ш. Южнее него в день июньского солнцестояния бывает полярная ночь, а в день декабрьского — полярный день.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP says beyond the polar circle the Sun is fully below the horizon on Midwinter’s Day and fully above on Midsummer’s Day (L315). It defines Antarctic Midwinter as the June winter solstice when the South Pole tilts maximally away from the Sun (L336), and Midsummer as the December summer solstice when the South Pole tilts maximally toward it (L339); therefore south of the Antarctic Circle June brings polar night and December brings polar day.
literalGroups.locator: AAP capture L315-L317,L334-L339; NOAA capture L12

literalGroups.literal: Северный полярный круг проходит примерно по 66,5° северной широты; за ним в день летнего солнцестояния Солнце не заходит.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Arctic Circle is at 66°34′N, and AAP says the Sun stays above the horizon beyond the circle on Midsummer’s Day. This supports the note’s northern latitude and summer condition.
literalGroups.locator: AAP capture L315; NOAA capture L12

literalGroups.literal: Тропик Рака проходит примерно по 23° северной широты и образует северную границу тропиков.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NOAA places the Tropic of Cancer at roughly 23°N and identifies it as the northern boundary of the tropics.

literalGroups.literal: Южнее этого круга в день декабрьского солнцестояния Солнце остаётся над горизонтом круглые сутки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP states that the Sun is above the horizon beyond the Antarctic Circle on Midsummer’s Day (L315); its Antarctic solstice definition places Midsummer on 21 or 22 December (L339), grounding the December daylight statement.

literalGroups.literal: Тропик Козерога проходит примерно по 23° южной широты и образует южную границу тропиков.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NOAA places the Tropic of Capricorn at roughly 23°S and identifies it as the southern boundary of the tropics.

Its own-option note states the correct northern solstice condition; it cannot satisfy southern Antarctica at 66.5°S.

correctNoteNewFact.fact: South of the Antarctic Circle, the Sun stays above the horizon through the December-solstice day (Antarctic Midsummer). This is an additional daylight fact beyond the prompt and key.
correctNoteNewFact.primaryLocator: Australian Antarctic Program retained capture L315,L337-L339. The page defines Antarctic Midsummer as the summer solstice on 21 or 22 December.
